notes.text: Venice text has Yosef pan Peksas and gives the concluding interpretation to the sages. It calls the son Nechunyah in narration and Chunya in direct speech.
The Vilna witness has Yosef Paskas, in agreement with the form quoted here.
Yerushalmi reads Yose ben Peksas and gives the verdict to the sages; it also preserves the debate about a living father’s limb.
The quoted biblical clause ends at בצדקו; the words that follow are the sages’ interpretation in Sifra and Yerushalmi.
The immediate witnesses give וצדקו עמו, a continuation of the interpretation on the righteous man’s merit.
The story as preserved in Sifra, Yerushalmi and Semachot has the sages apply the verse after hearing the case.
The sources describe a lesion on the leg that a physician cuts. The English general “growth” avoids assigning a specific diagnosis.
